<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
{(Lower boundedness and smoothness)}\label{TACO:L-smooth_assumption}
The objective function is lower bounded and $L$-smooth. That is, $F_{\star}:=\inf_W F(W)>-\infty$, and for all $W_1,W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the following holds: 
    $\| \nabla F(W_1) - \nabla F(W_2)\|_{(1,n\to 1,m)^*} \le L \|W_1 - W_2\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)}.$
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
{(Nonconvex convergence of vanilla TACO)}\label{thm:taco-convergence}
Let \Cref{TACO:L-smooth_assumption} hold and define $\Delta_F:= F(W_0)-F_{\star}$. The iterates $\{W_t\}_{t=0}^{T}$ in (\ref{eq:vanilla TACO update}) with step sizes $\eta_t>0$ satisfy
\begin{equation*}
    \min_{0\le t<T}\|\nabla F(W_t)\|_{(1,n\to1,m)^*}
    \le
    \frac{\Delta_F+\frac{L}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_t^2}
         {\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_t}.
\end{equation*}
In particular, with $\eta=\sqrt{\tfrac{2\Delta_F}{LT}}$, we have
    $
        \min_{0\le t<T} \|\nabla F(W_t)\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)^*}\le \sqrt{\frac{2L\Delta_F}{T}}.
    $
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- assumption-2: body_md -->
\label{ass:coherent}{(Coherent objective)} The objective depends on $W$ through the layer output, i.e., $F(W)=\phi(Wz)$ for a differentiable function $\phi:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end assumption-2 -->
<!-- assumption-3: body_md -->
\label{ass:attained}
{(Common target output)}
Starting from the same $W_0$, all compared methods converge to limits $W^\star$ satisfying
$
W^\star z=u^\star
$
for the same optimal output $u^\star$.
<!-- end assumption-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
({Adam and TACO continuation equivalence})\label{thm:adam-taco}
Let \Cref{ass:coherent,ass:attained} hold, and let the Adam Proxy follow (\ref{eq:adam-proxy}). Then both the TACO and Adam sequences lie in $\mathcal{C}(W_0,\operatorname{sign}(z))$ for all $t\geq 0$, and
$W_{\rm TACO}^\star=W_{\rm Adam}^\star=W_0+\frac{(u^\star-W_0z)\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top}{\|z\|_1}.$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
({Muon continuation separation})\label{thm:muon-sep}
Let \Cref{ass:coherent,ass:attained} hold and let the Muon proxy follow (\ref{eq:muon-proxy}). Further let $r=u^\star-W_0z$. Then Muon’s iterates lie in $\mathcal{C}(W_0,z)$ and
$W_{\rm Muon}^\star=W_0+\frac{rz^\top}{\|z\|_2^2}, W_{\rm Muon}^\star-W_{\rm TACO}^\star=r\left(\frac{z}{\|z\|_2^2}-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(z)}{\|z\|_1}\right)^\top.$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- assumption-4: body_md -->
\label{assum:winner_balance}{(Balanced TACO Winners)}
For $G\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, let $c_i$ denote the number of columns whose TACO winner lies in row $i$. We assume $\max_i c_i=\Theta(n/m)$ for all iterates $W_t$.
<!-- end assumption-4 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
{(TACO $\mu$P-scaling)}\label{thm:taco_mup}
Let \Cref{assum:winner_balance} hold. Then the TACO direction $D=\frac{m}{n}\mathcal{S}(G)$ satisfies $\|D\|_2=\frac{m}{n}\sqrt{\max_i c_i},$ for every $G$. Hence $D$ satisfies the standard $\mu$P spectral scaling
$
\|D\|_2=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{m}{n}}\right).
$
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
{(Nonconvex convergence of vanilla TACO)}
Let Assumption~\ref{TACO:L-smooth_assumption} hold and define $\Delta_F=F(W_0)-F_{\star}$. The iterates $\{W_t\}_{t=0}^{T}$ in (\ref{eq:vanilla TACO update}) with step size $\eta_t>0$ follow
\begin{equation*}
    \min_{0\le t<T}\|\nabla F(W_t)\|_{(1,n\to1,m)^*}
    \le
    \frac{\Delta_F+\frac{L}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_t^2}
         {\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_t}.
\end{equation*}
In particular, with $\eta=\sqrt{\tfrac{2\Delta_F}{LT}}$, we have
    $
        \min_{0\le t<T} \|\nabla F(W_t)\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)^*}\le \sqrt{\frac{2L\Delta_F}{T}}.
    $
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By Assumption \ref{TACO:L-smooth_assumption}, using the $L$-smoothness of $F$, for any update direction $D$, we have
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:desecent}
        F(W + D) \le F(W) + \left\langle \nabla F(W), D \right\rangle_F + \frac{L}{2} \|D\|_{(1,n\to 1,m)}^2.
    \end{equation}
    Since $\nabla F(W)=G,$ with $W_{t+1} = W_t - \eta_t D_t$, we have $\|D_t\|_{(1,n \to 1, m)} \le 1$, $\left\langle G_t, D_t \right\rangle_F = \|G_t\|_{(1,n\to 1,m)^*}$, and (\ref{eq:desecent}) reduces to
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:desecent1}
        F(W_{t+1}) \le F(W_t) - \eta_t \| G_t\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)^*} + \frac{L}{2} \eta_t^2.
    \end{equation}
    Summing (\ref{eq:desecent1}) with $t$ varying from $0$ to $T-1$ gives
    \begin{equation}
        F(W_T) - F(W_0) \le - \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \eta_t \| G_t\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)^*} + \frac{L}{2} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \eta_t^2.
    \end{equation}
    Note that $F \ge F_{\star}$. Reordering the inequality, we obtain
    \begin{equation}
        \left( \min_{t< T}\| G_t\|_{(1,n \to 1,m)^*} \right) \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \eta_t  \le \Delta F + \frac{L}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \eta_t^2,
    \end{equation}
    which proves the result.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
({Adam and TACO continuation equivalence})
Let \Cref{ass:coherent,ass:attained} hold, and let the Adam Proxy follow (\ref{eq:adam-proxy}). Then both the TACO and Adam sequences lie in $\mathcal{C}(W_0,\operatorname{sign}(z))$ for all $t\geq 0$, and
\[W_{\rm TACO}^\star=W_{\rm Adam}^\star=W_0+\frac{(u^\star-W_0z)\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top}{\|z\|_1}.\]
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Assumption~\ref{ass:coherent} and the chain rule give $G_t=\nabla F(W_t)=g_tz^\top$ with $g_t=\nabla\phi(W_tz)$.

For TACO,  $M_t=p_tz^\top$ for some $p_t\in\mathbb{R}^m$. This holds at $t=0$ since $M_{-1}=0$. If $M_{t-1}=p_{t-1}z^\top$, then $\mu M_{t-1}+(1-\mu)G_t=\tilde{p}_tz^\top$ with $\tilde{p}_t=\mu p_{t-1}+(1-\mu)g_t$. 

Column $j$ of $\tilde{p}_tz^\top$ equals $z_j\tilde{p}_t$, so its entry magnitudes are $|z_j||\tilde{p}_{t,i}|$ and their ordering does not depend on $j$.

The nonzero columns have the same magnitude ordering, with
equal-magnitude entries ordered by row index. Hence, $H_k$
retains the same row set $\mathcal I_t$ in each nonzero column,
while zero columns remain zero, giving $M_t=p_tz^\top$.

The same ordering argument applied to $S$ selects a single row $i_t^\star$ in every column with $z_j\neq 0$ and returns a zero column whenever $z_j=0$, so $S(M_t)=\operatorname{sign}(p_{t,i_t^\star})e_{i_t^\star}\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top$ and $D_t=\frac{m}{n}S(M_t)$ has the form $a\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top$.

For the Adam proxy,  $M_t=p_tz^\top$ and $V_t=q_t(z\odot z)^\top$ with $q_t\geq 0$ entrywise. Both hold at $t=0$ and propagate, since $G_t\odot G_t=(g_t\odot g_t)(z\odot z)^\top$. Bias correction preserves the two forms, so the $(i,j)$ entry of $\hat{M}_t/\sqrt{\hat{V}_t}$ equals $c_t(p_{t,i}/\sqrt{q_{t,i}})\operatorname{sign}(z_j)$ with $c_t=\sqrt{1-\beta_2^{t+1}}/(1-\beta_1^{t+1})$, giving an update of the form $a\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top$ as well.

Hence, both sequences lie in $\mathcal{C}(W_0,\operatorname{sign}(z))$. 

For $W=W_0+a\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top$ we have $\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top z=\|z\|_1$, hence $Wz=W_0z+a\|z\|_1$. Imposing $Wz=u^\star$ and using $\|z\|_1>0$ determines $a=(u^\star-W_0z)/\|z\|_1$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
({Muon continuation separation})
Let \Cref{ass:coherent,ass:attained} hold and let the Muon proxy follow (\ref{eq:muon-proxy}). Further let $r=u^\star-W_0z$. Then Muon's iterates lie in $\mathcal{C}(W_0,z)$ and
$$W_{\rm Muon}^\star=W_0+\frac{rz^\top}{\|z\|_2^2},\qquad W_{\rm Muon}^\star-W_{\rm TACO}^\star=r\left(\frac{z}{\|z\|_2^2}-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(z)}{\|z\|_1}\right)^\top.$$
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The gradient can be represented via $G_t=g_tz^\top$, and $B_t=b_tz^\top$ by induction from $B_{-1}=0$. 

If $b_t\neq 0$, then
$$ b_tz^\top=(b_t/\|b_t\|_2)(\|b_t\|_2\|z\|_2)(z/\|z\|_2)^\top $$
is a singular value decomposition, so $\mathcal{P}(B_t)=b_tz^\top/(\|b_t\|_2\|z\|_2)$.

Hence, every update has the form $az^\top$, so the iterates and their limit lie in the closed set $\mathcal{C}(W_0,z)$.

For $W=W_0+az^\top$ we have $Wz=W_0z+a\|z\|_2^2$, and $Wz=u^\star$ forces $a=r/\|z\|_2^2$, which gives the endpoint. 

Subtracting the endpoint of \Cref{thm:adam-taco} gives the displayed difference, and $z^\top z/\|z\|_2^2=\operatorname{sign}(z)^\top z/\|z\|_1=1$ gives $(W_{\rm Muon}^\star-W_{\rm TACO}^\star)z=0$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rmk:layerwise}{(Extension to deep neural networks)}
\Cref{thm:adam-taco} extends directly to deep networks under sequential layerwise fine-tuning. Consider
    
              
                                        
                         
    
$$
h_0=x,\qquad
h_\ell=\sigma_\ell(W^{(\ell)} h_{\ell-1}),
\qquad \ell=1,\ldots,L,
$$
and optimize one $W^{(\ell)}$ at a time while keeping all other layers fixed. During each stage, $h_{\ell-1}$ is fixed, so the objective depends on $W^{(\ell)}$ only through $W^{(\ell)} h_{\ell-1}$ and therefore satisfies \Cref{ass:coherent} with $z=h_{\ell-1}$. \Cref{thm:adam-taco} then implies that TACO and the Adam proxy reach the same endpoint for that layer. Since the resulting networks are identical, they produce the same input to the next layer, and repeating this argument over $\ell=1,\ldots,L$ yields identical final networks.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
{(TACO $\mu$P-scaling)}
                         
Let \Cref{assum:winner_balance} hold. Then the TACO direction $D=\frac{m}{n}\mathcal{S}(G)$ satisfies $\|D\|_2=\frac{m}{n}\sqrt{\max_i c_i},$ for every $G$. Hence $D$ satisfies the standard $\mu$P spectral scaling
$
\|D\|_2=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{m}{n}}\right).
$
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Since each column of $\mathcal{S}(G)$ contains one nonzero entry at row $i_j$, we have
$$
\mathcal{S}(G)\mathcal{S}(G)^\top=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_m).
$$
Hence,
$$
\|\mathcal{S}(G)\|_2=\sqrt{\max_i c_i},
$$
and the TACO direction $D=\frac{m}{n}\mathcal{S}(G)$ satisfies
$$
\|D\|_2=\frac{m}{n}\sqrt{\max_i c_i}.
$$
This identity holds for every $G$ and uses no assumptions. Dividing by $\sqrt{m/n}$ gives
$$
\frac{\|D\|_2}{\sqrt{m/n}}=\sqrt{\frac{m}{n}\max_i c_i},
$$
so the left side is $\Theta(1)$ exactly when $\max_i c_i=\Theta(n/m)$, which proves both directions.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
({Winner-margin preservation of TACO})
\label{thm:taco-exact-history}
 Let
$i^\star_{t,j}=\arg\max_i|\tilde M_{t,ij}|$ and define the dense-history
winner margin as
$
\gamma_{t,j}
=
|\tilde M_{t,i^\star_{t,j},j}|
-
\max_{i\neq i^\star_{t,j}}|\tilde M_{t,ij}|.
$
If $\gamma_{t,j}>2\varepsilon_{t,j}$ for every column $j$ and iteration $t$,
then $\mathcal{S}(M_t)=\mathcal{S}(\tilde M_t)$ for all $t\geq0$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Fix a column $j$ and iteration $t$, and let
$i^\star=i^\star_{t,j}$. Then,
$$
|M_{t,i^\star j}|
\geq
|\tilde M_{t,i^\star j}|-\varepsilon_{t,j}.
$$
For any $i\neq i^\star$,
$$
|M_{t,ij}|
\leq
|\tilde M_{t,ij}|+\varepsilon_{t,j}.
$$
Since $\gamma_{t,j}>2\varepsilon_{t,j}$,
$$
|\tilde M_{t,i^\star j}|-\varepsilon_{t,j}
>
\max_{i\neq i^\star}|\tilde M_{t,ij}|+\varepsilon_{t,j}.
$$
Therefore,
$$
|M_{t,i^\star j}|>|M_{t,ij}|
$$
for every $i\neq i^\star$, so the dense and sparse gradient histories select the same winning row.

Moreover, $\gamma_{t,j}>2\varepsilon_{t,j}$ implies
$|\tilde M_{t,i^\star j}|>\varepsilon_{t,j}$. Hence,
$$
|M_{t,i^\star j}-\tilde M_{t,i^\star j}|
\leq\varepsilon_{t,j}
<
|\tilde M_{t,i^\star j}|,
$$
so the selected entries also have the same sign. By the definition of
$\mathcal{S}$ in equation~(4),
$$
\mathcal{S}(M_t)_{:,j}
=
\mathcal{S}(\tilde M_t)_{:,j}.
$$
Since this holds for every column $j$, we obtain
$$
\mathcal{S}(M_t)=\mathcal{S}(\tilde M_t)
$$
for all $t\geq0$, which proves the result.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
